stem: Priya starts at point P facing East. She walks 6 km, turns left, walks 4 km, turns left, walks 6 km, and stops at point Q. How far is Q from P, and in which direction is Q from P?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Path: East 6 km -> turn left (now North) 4 km -> turn left (now West) 6 km. Net displacement: East 6 - West 6 = 0 horizontal, North 4 km. Q is 4 km North of P.
Treating a left turn from East as South (instead of North) gives 4 km South, a turn-direction error.
Reporting only the last leg (6 km West) as the displacement ignores the North 4 km segment and the cancellation of East and West legs.
Adding all distances walked (6+4+6 = 16 km) instead of computing net displacement, with a wrong South direction, produces 16 or 12 km South.

explanation: Map the path on a coordinate grid. Starting at origin facing East: move (6,0), turn left to face North, move (6,4), turn left to face West, move (0,4). Net: 0 East-West, 4 North. Q is 4 km North of P.

explanation_sections.punchline: East and West legs cancel; only the North segment contributes to net displacement.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: set up a coordinate system. Left turn from East is North; left turn from North is West. Final position: x = 6 - 6 = 0, y = 4. Distance = 4 km, direction = North.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always convert turns to absolute compass directions, then compute net x and y components; do not sum path lengths.
explanation_sections.timing: About 60-75 seconds. The trap is the direction-turn error at the first left turn from East, which gives South instead of North.
